sources.publisher: Central Ground Water Board via India-WRIS

conventions.depth_sign: WRIS sign convention is PER STATION, not per dataset: telemetric wells report depth-to-water NEGATIVE while manual wells report it positive. Rejecting v<0 as invalid drops 9,115 readings and makes Kolkata look groundwater-dead since 2023. Sign is normalised per station, never globally.
conventions.station_metadata: Station lat/lng is taken from the first row that carries it, NOT the latest row: WRIS leaves coordinates null on many recent rows, and a latest-row read collapses Nadia from 205 wells to 39 while the remainder still look plausible.

source: Central Ground Water Board, via the India-WRIS Ground Water Level API
cadence_note: Raw cadence is a mix of 6-hourly telemetric and periodic manual readings; published here as monthly means.
notes: Kolkata is NOT groundwater-poor: 23 stations in the district and 667 across the six KMA districts, denser per area than Delhi's 237-well network.
Districts marked stale have genuinely stopped reporting and are shown as such rather than interpolated over.
A narrow date window or an unpaged request understates the network badly: Kolkata reads as 3 stations either way, against 23 when paged to exhaustion.
